subject: Post-demo: grounding thresholds, reranker choice & next steps for ClarifyRx pilot
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Kira Patel <kira@clarifyrx.com>; Dr. Sean Meyers <sean.m@clarifyrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + recommended next steps (grounding & reranker)

Hi Kira / Sean —

Thanks again for carving out time today — really appreciated the demo and the clarity on the three core success criteria: (1) accurate citations for medication guidance, (2) sub-second median latency for point-of-care queries, and (3) a clear audit trail for any content used in patient-facing recommendations.

Quick recap of what we covered and what Redwood recommends as the minimal eval scope to qualify for a pilot: 

- Evaluation focus: grounding precision (precision@cite), hallucination rate (free-text hallucinations per 100 responses), and latency under target throughput.
- Suggested models to benchmark: Redwood-7B-quant (baseline, lowest-cost), Llama3-13B-4bit (balanced accuracy/latency), and Falcon-40B-8bit (upper bound for accuracy).
- Retrieval stack proposal: FAISS (HNSW) index with text-embedding-ada-like embeddings for initial retrieval; retrieval params to try: top_k = 50 for recall-oriented probes, top_p reranking window = 10 for production candidate set.
- Reranker recommendation: run a two-stage experiment: (A) lightweight bi-encoder (SBERT-mpnet-base-v2) for speed; (B) cross-encoder (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) for quality baseline. Cross-encoder to be used to measure upper-bound grounded precision for gating decisions.
- Prompt sets: attached is a first-pass prompt set (clarify-promptset-v1.json) with explicit citation instructions and a conservative "do not hallucinate" guardrail. Please review and flag any clinical language that might be too restrictive for your triage flows.

Next steps we propose (short timeline):
1) You review the attached prompt set and drop comments in the Drive doc by EOD Wednesday (2027-07-21).
2) Redwood runs benchmark sweep (models & retriever/reranker combos) against your 250-case evaluation deck next week; we'll share a summary CSV + evaluation notebook.
3) Align on grounding threshold: we suggest starting threshold = 0.85 precision@cite and tolerance of 5 hallucinations / 100 responses. We can relax/tighten after the first sweep.
4) Schedule an ops sync (30m) to discuss staging endpoints and SSO/access for your engineers (proposed: Thu 2027-07-22).

Attachments: clarify-promptset-v1.json, benchmark-results-20270715.csv (sample from comparable pilot), eval-harness-instructions.md

I'll loop in Marissa and Ben for the sweep execution and relay a short runbook once the scope is finalized.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Kira Patel <kira@clarifyrx.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Sean Meyers <sean.m@clarifyrx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended next steps (grounding & reranker)

Vanessa — thanks, this is great and in-line with what our clinicians emphasized. A couple quick clarifications before we review the prompt set: 

1) For the "precision@cite" metric you propose, are you measuring that only when the system returns an explicit citation (i.e., cite tokens present), or across all responses (implicit precision)? We care most about explicit citations being correct.

2) On retriever fast config: can you confirm indexing cadence? Our knowledge base updates hourly (lab results, drug advisories). Would FAISS HNSW handle that frequency without a full rebuild?

3) Can Ben/Marissa include a short note in the benchmark summary about tokenization differences you expect between the models (we want to understand cost implications for long clinical notes).

We'll review the promptset and comment in Drive by Wed. If the threshold is 0.85 precision@cite, what are you using as the cross-encoder score cutoff to trigger a human-in-loop?

Thanks — Kira
Director of Product, ClarifyRx
kira@clarifyrx.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kira Patel <kira@clarifyrx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended next steps (grounding & reranker)

Kira — quick answers, and a few implementation notes for the sweep: 

1) precision@cite: we will measure precision only on responses that include an explicit citation token. We'll also surface a separate metric, "response-coverage", that shows fraction of queries that include any citation. That should map to your "explicit citation" requirement.

2) Indexing cadence: HNSW in FAISS supports incremental adds without a full rebuild; for hourly updates we recommend a short batching window (5–10 min) with a lightweight merge job. We'll include a config to do asynchronous incremental updates and surface staleness windows in the benchmark.

3) Tokenization/cost: we'll include token breakdowns per model in the CSV. Expect ~1.6x token count moving from the Redwood-7B to Llama3-13B due to tokenizer differences and prompt context lengths. We'll include projected per-100k token costs for your committed throughput.

Cross-encoder cutoff: for the sweep we'll report calibrated cross-encoder scores and propose a conservative production cutoff (e.g., cross-encoder score >= 0.72) to automatically surface an answer; below that we send to human review. That cutoff is a starting point — we'll tune against your 250-case deck.

Implementation notes for the reranker experiment:
- Candidate pipeline: retriever(top_k=50) -> bi-encoder re-rank -> cross-encoder re-rank (for labeled eval only).
- Grounding metrics: precision@cite, recall@k (k=10,50), MRR@10, and hallucination-rate. We'll produce both aggregated metrics and per-case flags for clinician review.
- We recommend running the cross-encoder only in the evaluation path. For production, if latency budget is tight, use bi-encoder + light calibration for gating.

I'll kick off the benchmark sweep on Wed morning once Kira confirms prompt edits; benchmark artifacts will land in the Drive folder and I'll drop a summary link in this thread.

— Ben
Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Kira Patel <kira@clarifyrx.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended next steps (grounding & reranker)

Thanks, Ben — that covers the questions I had. We've left initial comments on the prompt set in Drive (two small edits to the citation phrasing and one example where clinical context should be preserved).

Confirming: ClarifyRx approves the benchmark sweep. Please proceed with Redwood-7B-quant and Llama3-13B-4bit runs, and include Falcon-40B-8bit as a quality ceiling. We'll expect the results and the proposed cross-encoder cutoff by EOD next Monday (2027-07-26).

Kira
Director of Product, ClarifyRx
